competitions.result: Community Shield runners-up — lost 1–0 to Arsenal.
Fourth round — lost 2–0 at home to Crystal Palace in a replay.
Winners — beat Manchester United 2–0 in Cardiff.
Champions League first group phase — third in Group B; transferred to the UEFA Cup.
Quarter-final — lost 3–1 on aggregate to Celtic.

in.note: Joined in May 2002 ahead of the new campaign.

out.note: Left on 13 May 2002 after the previous campaign.

overview: Liverpool won the League Cup but slipped to fifth in the Premier League with 64 points. Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2–0 final victory over Manchester United in Cardiff on 2 March. Liverpool had been unbeaten in their opening 12 league matches, but then went 11 without a league win.

Their Champions League campaign ended in the first group phase, with a 3–3 draw at Basel leaving them third in the group. They continued in the UEFA Cup before Celtic won their quarter-final 3–1 on aggregate. Crystal Palace knocked Liverpool out of the FA Cup in a fourth-round replay, winning 2–0 at Anfield.

Owen again finished as leading scorer with 28 competitive goals. Summer arrivals included El Hadji Diouf, Salif Diao and Bruno Cheyrou, while Gary McAllister, Nick Barmby and Jari Litmanen left. A 2–1 defeat at Chelsea on the final league day left Liverpool three points behind their opponents in fourth place.

The opening 12-match unbeaten league run and subsequent 11-match winless league run are counted separately from cup fixtures. Cup victories during the latter period mean it must not be described as an all-competition winless run.

The UEFA Cup fifth round was the quarter-final. The renamed Community Shield retains the existing charity-shield identity; its contemporary name appears in the result. Anelka’s loan departure was already recorded with the previous season.
